title: Make egg-internal tools discoverable to sandbox agents via an in-process SDK MCP server
revision_reason: v1 was ACKed by reviewer_plan but never CONFIRMED (architect container exited 1). v2 re-proposes after aligning concrete choices with the confirmed task_planner plan at .egg-state/drafts/1765-plan.md (commit 974832e75) and addressing reviewer_plan's six non-blocking comments (flag default, namespace split, SDK pin, nudge derivation, TD8 note, optional peer fields). Architectural conclusions are unchanged — only configuration-level choices were reconciled with the final plan.
summary: Implement an in-process Claude Agent SDK MCP server (Hybrid D + prompt nudge) that exposes 15 semantic-verb tools (BRC lifecycle, HITL registration, progress/heartbeat, task completion, phase orientation) to sandbox agents. The server is built in shared/egg_agent/client.py via claude_agent_sdk.create_sdk_mcp_server() and wired onto ClaudeAgentOptions.mcp_servers when EGG_MCP_TOOLS=true (opt-in, default off for iteration 1 burn-in). Tool @tool wrappers call pure handler functions extracted from sandbox/egg_lib/contract_cli.py and orch_cli.py into sandbox/egg_agent_tools/handlers/ so CLIs and MCP tools share one source of truth. A short (~150-word) bootstrap paragraph — generated programmatically from the TOOL_NAMESPACES registry at import time so it cannot drift — is appended to options.system_prompt in the same flag-gated block. Works identically in public and private network modes (zero new network surface, zero new ports, zero new processes). claude_agent_sdk harness only; EGG_HARNESS=egg coverage is deferred to iteration 2 per decision-3. Existing sandbox/bin/egg-* CLIs stay intact per decision-4.

hitl_decisions_incorporated.decision-2_handler_derivation: Hybrid — argparse-skeleton auto-derivation via schemas.derive_schema_from_argparse() with per-tool override hooks (build_tool_schema(tool_name, overrides=None)). Tools without a CLI counterpart declare their schema directly.
hitl_decisions_incorporated.decision-3_harness_coverage: claude_agent_sdk harness only for iteration 1. shared/egg_harness/ (EGG_HARNESS=egg) is unchanged; parallel registration tracked for iteration 2 when the experimental harness graduates.
hitl_decisions_incorporated.decision-4_cli_retention: sandbox/bin/egg-* CLIs retained indefinitely. Humans, tests, and bash recovery wrappers see zero behaviour change — argparse parser definition, stdout text, and exit codes are preserved byte-for-byte.
hitl_decisions_incorporated.decision-5_SUPERSEDED: Superseded by decision-7. Earlier CLI-mirroring naming (mcp__egg_contract__add_decision) rejected.
hitl_decisions_incorporated.decision-6_SUPERSEDED: Superseded by decision-8. Earlier full-breadth scoping rejected.
hitl_decisions_incorporated.decision-7_naming: Semantic verb-based names grouped by agent function: mcp__sdlc__* (3), mcp__brc__* (6), mcp__phase__* (2), mcp__progress__* (3), mcp__task__* (1). FIVE namespaces total — aligned with TASK-2-2 in the companion plan.
hitl_decisions_incorporated.decision-8_iter1_scope: BRC + HITL + phase-context + progress + task-completion core = 15 verbs. Full capability audit (~15 additional verbs — peer, checkpoint, anchor, overseer, task-gap) tracked in follow-up #1917.

architecture_overview.shape: One in-process SDK MCP server per agent process, registered at agent spawn time in shared/egg_agent/client.py::run_agent_async. The server aggregates all 15 iteration-1 tools under a single server name (`egg`) — SDK-exposed names become `mcp__egg__<verb>`… see TD1 below for why the server-name-level split was consciously traded away. Tools are async Python functions decorated with @tool; their wrappers call pure-Python handler functions in sandbox/egg_agent_tools/handlers/ via asyncio.to_thread. Those same handler functions are the destination of refactored argparse cmd_* entry points in sandbox/egg_lib/contract_cli.py and orch_cli.py, so CLI and MCP tool share one code path.
control_flow: 1. Orchestrator spawns a sandbox Job (kubernetes_spawner.py / container_spawner.py) which runs `python3 -m egg_agent <prompt>` with EGG_* env vars set.

3. run_agent_async builds ClaudeAgentOptions (lines 194-208 today). **NEW**: gated on `os.environ.get('EGG_MCP_TOOLS') == 'true'`, it lazy-imports sandbox.egg_agent_tools.build_sandbox_mcp_server(), constructs the in-process SDK MCP server, and assigns `options.mcp_servers = {'egg': server}`.

4. **NEW**: In the same flag-gated block, run_agent_async concatenates sandbox.egg_agent_tools.SYSTEM_PROMPT_NUDGE (derived at import from TOOL_NAMESPACES) onto the effective options.system_prompt (preserving any caller prompt).
5. claude_agent_sdk.query() surfaces `mcp__egg__<verb>` names to Claude alongside Bash/Read/Edit/etc., with the TypedDict/JSON-schema input validated before the handler runs.
6. When Claude invokes a tool, the SDK dispatches in-process to the @tool-decorated async wrapper in the same Python process (no network, same PID, same env vars).

7. The wrapper runs the sync handler via asyncio.to_thread(handler, req) so that blocking urllib gateway I/O does not freeze the event loop, catches GatewayError/TimeoutError/Exception, and returns either the handler's dict (serialised per SDK contract) or `{is_error: True, content: [{type: 'text', text: <message>}]}`.

8. **Flag-off path**: when EGG_MCP_TOOLS is unset or 'false', none of steps 3–4 execute. The SDK call is byte-for-byte identical to today — preserving AC 'existing CLIs keep working' for pipelines that have not opted in.
architecture_overview.private_mode_behavior: Zero net-new network. All tool dispatch happens in the sandbox container's own Python interpreter. Tools that talk to the orchestrator (brc_propose → POST /consensus, progress_emit → POST /progress) reuse the existing urllib round-trip through the gateway sidecar, which is already the supported path for both public and private modes. Public vs private network mode is irrelevant to tool discovery and to tool invocation — discovery is SDK-internal and dispatch is in-process.
architecture_overview.authz_model: Authz is by construction: the sandbox agent process imports only sandbox.egg_agent_tools. It physically cannot name `submit_task` or `cancel_task` because those symbols live in orchestrator/mcp_tools.py and are not part of the sandbox image's import path. Gateway-enforced role restrictions (existing today for the CLI commands those handlers wrap) continue to authorize the HTTP calls; no new authz layer is introduced.

new_package_sandbox_egg_agent_tools.purpose: Sandbox-process-only package defining the agent-facing MCP tool surface, the bootstrap nudge, and the server factory. Lives under sandbox/ (not shared/) because only the sandbox agent imports it — reviewer_agent_design feedback from refine explicitly recommended sandbox/ over shared/ for authz-by-construction.

layout_final.__init__.py: Public surface: exports build_sandbox_mcp_server(), TOOL_NAMESPACES (ordered dict {namespace: [tool_name, ...]}), SYSTEM_PROMPT_NUDGE (rendered at import).
layout_final.server.py: Factory: build_sandbox_mcp_server() returns an SdkMcpServer via claude_agent_sdk.create_sdk_mcp_server(name='egg', tools=[...all 15 @tool fns...]). Single aggregate server per TD1 rationale (simpler ClaudeAgentOptions wiring, SDK doesn't care about server-name split for tool naming).
layout_final.schemas.py: derive_schema_from_argparse(subparser) → JSON-schema inputSchema. build_tool_schema(tool_name, overrides=None) merges auto-derived skeleton with per-tool overrides. Tools without a CLI counterpart (5 of 15) declare their schema inline.
layout_final.handlers/sdlc.py: Pure sync functions register_open_question(req), request_feedback(req), check_hitl_answers(req). Each takes a plain dict, returns a plain dict, raises GatewayError on HTTP failure — never sys.exit.
layout_final.handlers/brc.py: Pure sync functions brc_propose, brc_ack, brc_nack, brc_confirm, brc_get_state, brc_list_blocking. brc_get_state accepts verbose:bool for large-payload truncation per feedback-Q4. brc_list_blocking is a derived view over the structured state.
layout_final.handlers/phase.py: Pure sync functions phase_get_context, phase_get_assigned_tasks. See phase_context_data_model below.
layout_final.handlers/progress.py: Pure sync functions progress_emit, progress_signal_error, progress_heartbeat.
layout_final.handlers/task.py: Pure sync function task_complete (split from sdlc per decision-7's semantic verb naming).
layout_final.tools/__init__.py: Imports every namespace module and builds the single SDK tool list that server.py registers. Declares TOOL_NAMESPACES = {'sdlc': [...], 'brc': [...], 'phase': [...], 'progress': [...], 'task': [...]} which is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for both the @tool decorator registrations and the SYSTEM_PROMPT_NUDGE text.
layout_final.tools/sdlc.py: @tool-decorated async wrappers for every handlers.sdlc.* function. Each wrapper: (a) validates input, (b) runs handler via asyncio.to_thread, (c) catches GatewayError/TimeoutError/Exception → {is_error: True, content: [...]}, (d) on success serialises handler dict per SDK contract, (e) declares cli_command=('egg-contract', 'add-decision') style attribute where a CLI counterpart exists (omitted/None for the 5 new-capability tools).
layout_final.tools/brc.py: Same pattern for handlers.brc.*. Tools brc_get_state and brc_list_blocking have cli_command=None (new capabilities).
layout_final.tools/phase.py: Same pattern for handlers.phase.*. Both tools have cli_command=None (new capabilities).
layout_final.bootstrap.py: Renders SYSTEM_PROMPT_NUDGE at module import by iterating TOOL_NAMESPACES — one-bullet-per-namespace + one-line description derived from a hand-curated per-namespace help dict. Drift-proof: adding a namespace to TOOL_NAMESPACES automatically extends the nudge on next import. A Phase-4 symmetric drift test asserts every mcp__<namespace>__ substring in the rendered nudge maps to a registered namespace and vice versa.

new_package_sandbox_egg_agent_tools.rationale_for_single_package: The concurrent task_planner plan co-locates handlers with tool wrappers under one package (sandbox/egg_agent_tools/) rather than the earlier architect-output split (sandbox/egg_lib/{contract,orch}_handlers.py). This simplifies: (a) the drift-prevention CI test (one package to scan for (cli_command, handler_fn) pairs), (b) the lazy-import boundary in run_agent_async (one package to guard), (c) the developer mental model (agent-MCP-tool code is one directory). Per TD2 below, this trade-off was made consciously; CLI argparse dispatchers keep calling into this package the same way external Python callers would.

changes: make_gateway_request (lines 239-291) refactored to raise a dedicated GatewayError exception on HTTPError/URLError/TimeoutError instead of calling sys.exit(1) at lines 284/288/291. This is a hard prerequisite for the handlers — handlers MUST NEVER call sys.exit because in the @tool async context that would kill the agent interpreter.

cmd_add_decision (line 736) becomes a thin argparse-to-request shim that calls handlers.sdlc.register_open_question(req), prints today's stdout text from the dict response, catches GatewayError and renders the existing stderr + exit code for human callers.
refactor_contract_cli.invariant: Argparse parser definition (create_parser, set_defaults), stdout text, and exit codes are byte-identical to today. Snapshot tests in Phase 4 enforce this. Humans, tests, and bash recovery scripts see zero behaviour change.

changes: cmd_consensus_status (line 1483) → refactored so its structured-data build is factored into handlers.brc.brc_get_state (returning full JSON including verbose=True payload). The existing text-rendering stdout path in the CLI keeps its current shape by consuming the dict.
refactor_orch_cli.invariant: Same as contract_cli — no change to argparse surface, stdout text, or exit codes. Snapshot tests enforce this.

changes: In run_agent_async, after the ClaudeAgentOptions(...) construction at line 194 and before line 209, add a flag-gated block: `if os.environ.get('EGG_MCP_TOOLS') == 'true': from sandbox.egg_agent_tools import build_sandbox_mcp_server, SYSTEM_PROMPT_NUDGE; options.mcp_servers = {'egg': build_sandbox_mcp_server()}; options.system_prompt = (options.system_prompt or '') + '\n\n' + SYSTEM_PROMPT_NUDGE`.

The import is lazy (inside the if-branch) so the non-MCP code path has zero dependency on the sandbox.egg_agent_tools package — shared/egg_agent/ can be consumed by non-sandbox callers without pulling in handler modules.
An ImportError guard around the lazy import is not needed — if the flag is on but the package is missing, that is a deployment bug and should fail loudly.
Log tool registration to the structured event logger so checkpoint browsing shows an `agent_tools_registered` event at session init.
shared_egg_agent_client_changes.minimal_diff_estimate: ~12 lines added, no existing lines changed. Flag-off path is byte-identical to today.

phase_context_data_model.purpose: phase_get_context is the new orientation tool. It reads env vars (EGG_PIPELINE_ID, EGG_AGENT_ROLE, EGG_ISSUE_NUMBER, EGG_BRANCH, EGG_REPO_PATH, EGG_NETWORK_MODE), the contract JSON via the gateway, and existing .egg-state/drafts/ / .egg-state/agent-outputs/ paths, and returns one dict the agent reads on its first turn. This replaces the 5-tool-call archaeology pattern from the issue.
returned_fields_required: assigned_tasks: list[TaskRef]  # filtered from contract.phases[current].tasks by role
returned_fields_optional_best_effort: active_peers: list[{role, readiness_state}]  # best-effort; populated from BRC state if gateway call succeeds, else omitted
reviewer_peers: list[str]  # best-effort; populated from review_graph.get_review_graph_for_phase if gateway call succeeds, else omitted
hitl_pending: list[{id, kind, question}]  # best-effort; populated from unresolved decisions/feedback if gateway call succeeds, else omitted
phase_context_data_model.optional_field_rationale: Per reviewer_plan non-blocking feedback on iteration-1 scope (decision-8 listed phase_get_context as 'orientation bundle', not 'structured peer view'), the three peer-adjacent fields are marked best-effort in the handler signature so implementation can ship with a minimal required payload and grow in iteration 2 without breaking agent callers. When a gateway call for optional data fails with any non-critical error, the handler logs a warning and omits the field from the response dict rather than raising.
phase_context_data_model.replaces: The agent's manual reconstruction via `echo $EGG_PIPELINE_ID`, `egg-contract show`, `egg-orch consensus status`, `ls .egg-state/drafts/` — a major source of tool-call burn on every agent's first few turns.
phase_context_data_model.planned_follow_ups: brc_peer_read_artifact (iteration 2 / #1917): lets reviewers fetch a producer's proposed artifact by BRC round without globbing .egg-state/brc-history/. Currently a 1–2 tool-call burn for reviewers; not critical-path but captured as valued capability for #1917 per reviewer_plan feedback.

iteration_1_tool_list_note: Tool names above follow the actual SDK exposure pattern `mcp__<server_name>__<tool_name>` where server_name='egg' (single aggregate server per TD1). The `namespace` field groups tools logically and drives the SYSTEM_PROMPT_NUDGE grouping — the SDK itself only sees the flat list of 15 tool_names under one server. Aligned with TASK-2-2 in the companion plan (.egg-state/drafts/1765-plan.md).

runtime_dependencies.mcp: Present in the sandbox image transitively via claude-agent-sdk and directly as `mcp[cli]>=1.20.0` in sandbox/pyproject.toml. No change needed.
runtime_dependencies.claude_agent_sdk: Exposes tool(), create_sdk_mcp_server(), and ClaudeAgentOptions.mcp_servers. Verified at /usr/local/lib/python3.13/dist-packages/claude_agent_sdk/__init__.py:302 (0.1.65 installed in current sandbox).
runtime_dependencies.asyncio.to_thread: Used to wrap sync gateway-backed handler functions. Python 3.9+; we're on 3.13.

version_pinning.sandbox_pyproject_toml: Pin `claude-agent-sdk>=0.1.65,<0.2` (currently bare line 9 in sandbox/pyproject.toml). Pre-1.0 SDK can break between releases — a bounded range with an import smoke test catches breakage loudly at CI time rather than silently at agent-spawn time. Addresses risk-analyst R2 and reviewer_plan's §dependencies_and_constraints.version_pinning feedback.

dependencies_and_constraints.no_new_pypi_dependencies: Satisfies AC 'works in both public and private network modes' — no new pip install step at runtime. All required packages baked into the sandbox image.
dependencies_and_constraints.system_prompt_budget: Bootstrap nudge is static ~150 words (~200 input tokens/turn) per the rendered output in the plan. Gated by EGG_MCP_TOOLS, so flag-off pipelines pay zero. Observability in Phase 5 measures per-turn input-token cost with flag on vs off.
dependencies_and_constraints.no_new_ports: In-process means no listening socket. No new firewall rule, no new k8s Service, no new ingress.
dependencies_and_constraints.no_authz_changes_required: Sandbox-scoped tools never include submit_task / cancel_task / restart_phase. Gateway continues to authorize the HTTP calls the handlers make, using the same role-based rules in force today for the CLI commands.
dependencies_and_constraints.harness_coverage: claude_agent_sdk only in iteration 1. EGG_HARNESS=egg (shared/egg_harness/tools/) continues to call CLI subprocess as today until iteration 2 registers the same handlers against its tool registry. Caveat documented in docs/reference/agent-tools.md.

backward_compatibility.shell_clis: Every sandbox/bin/egg-* binary continues to work unchanged — they are argparse adapters over the extracted handlers. Snapshot tests in tests/sandbox/test_{contract,orch}_cli_parity.py lock stdout text + exit codes.
backward_compatibility.checkpoint_browser: Bash calls become mcp__egg__<tool> tool_use blocks. The checkpoint browser groups tool_use by name already (sandbox/egg_lib/checkpoint_cli.py); no schema change. `egg-checkpoint list --tool mcp__egg__brc_propose` works out of the box.

alternatives_considered.option_A_aggregated_docs: Rejected at HITL (decision-1). Does not change tool-call shape — agent still pays the argparse round-trip per invocation. Mitigates 'I don't know what exists' but not 'I don't know how to invoke it' — the second half of the issue's pain.
alternatives_considered.option_B_tool_manifest_in_prompt: Rejected as standalone at HITL. Partially adopted as the nudge component of the hybrid. Full manifest injection (every tool's full schema) would burn ~2k tokens/turn on a surface SDK-native discovery already provides.
alternatives_considered.option_C_second_mcp_server: Rejected at HITL. Adds network dependency, a second long-running process, and a new trust boundary. Tools execute outside the sandbox → they lose the agent's env vars (EGG_PIPELINE_ID, cwd) and every tool grows explicit-arg boilerplate. In-process wins on every criterion (network neutrality, authz by construction, latency, ops burden).
alternatives_considered.option_D_variant_one_server_per_namespac: Rejected by task_planner plan after architect v1 proposed it. Per-namespace servers yield `mcp__sdlc__*` directly, but the SDK does not care — the same agent-visible naming grouping is achievable via tool-name prefixing (`mcp__egg__sdlc_*`) under a single aggregate server. Aggregate is strictly simpler to wire (one ClaudeAgentOptions.mcp_servers entry) and keeps checkpoint-log tool grouping clean. If per-namespace gating becomes useful later (e.g. reviewer-only role disables `mcp__egg__progress_*`), the aggregate can split without agent-facing API churn.
alternatives_considered.alternative_naming_cli_mirrored: Rejected at HITL decision-7. CLI taxonomy (egg_contract, egg_orch) leaks binary organization into the agent's mental model. Semantic verbs are stable under CLI refactors and let new capabilities (brc_get_state, brc_list_blocking, phase_get_context) slot in without needing a new binary.
alternatives_considered.alternative_scope_everything: Rejected at HITL decision-8. ~30 tools in iteration 1 is too much surface to get right. BRC+HITL+phase-context+progress+task core (15) covers every agent role's critical-path action. Iteration 2 (#1917) picks up peer / checkpoint / anchor / overseer verbs.
alternatives_considered.inside_sandbox_mcp_server_daemon: Explicitly rejected by the issue itself (Option C variant). Long-running process inside the untrusted sandbox is an architectural outlier — doesn't compose with the existing orchestrator-hosted MCP pattern and adds a failure mode. In-process SDK MCP is the correct shape.
alternatives_considered.handler_location_egg_lib: Rejected by task_planner plan after architect v1 proposed sandbox/egg_lib/{contract,orch}_handlers.py. Co-locating handlers with CLI source files co-locates by mechanism (CLI) rather than by purpose (agent tooling). sandbox/egg_agent_tools/handlers/ co-locates handlers with their tool wrappers, simplifies the drift-prevention test (one package to scan), and keeps run_agent_async's lazy-import boundary clean.

recommended_approach.one_line: In-process Claude Agent SDK MCP server (single aggregate 'egg' server with 15 semantic-verb tools), sharing backing handlers with the existing CLIs via extracted pure functions, wired into shared/egg_agent/client.py behind EGG_MCP_TOOLS (opt-in, default off for iteration 1), and complemented by a programmatically-rendered system-prompt nudge that cannot drift from the tool registry.
why_this_wins: Architectural consistency: the codepath already constructs ClaudeAgentOptions. Adding mcp_servers is the smallest possible new surface (~12 LOC in client.py).
Single source of truth for CLI ↔ MCP: both dispatch to the same pure handler function, so new capabilities ship in one PR and both consumers immediately see them.
Network-mode neutrality: in-process means public and private modes are identical. No network decision needed.
Authz by construction: sandbox agent process cannot name tools that don't exist in its import path. No new trust boundary.
Capability-audit-driven semantic names: agents see `register_open_question` matching their mental model, not `add-decision` mirroring a binary's subcommand.

Programmatic nudge with symmetric drift test: nudge is rendered at import from TOOL_NAMESPACES — adding/renaming/removing a namespace updates the nudge automatically; drift CI test asserts the mapping is bijective.
No new long-running process, no new port, no new k8s Service, no new auth token, no new network egress.
Flag-gated opt-in for burn-in: flag-off path is byte-identical to today. Zero regression risk for pipelines that don't set EGG_MCP_TOOLS=true.

phase_1_handler_extraction.description: Extract pure-Python handler functions from cmd_* in contract_cli.py and orch_cli.py. Each cmd_X becomes a thin argparse shim around handler X. make_gateway_request refactored to raise GatewayError instead of sys.exit. New-capability handlers (check_hitl_answers, brc_get_state, brc_list_blocking, phase_get_context, phase_get_assigned_tasks) added.
phase_1_handler_extraction.test_approach: Unit test per handler: happy-path, missing-env-var, gateway-5xx (asserting GatewayError raised, NOT sys.exit called). Existing CLI regression tests (tests/sandbox/test_brc_cli_args.py, test_overseer_alert_cli.py) continue to pass. Snapshot tests in test_{contract,orch}_cli_parity.py lock stdout + exit codes with committed fixtures (no first-run auto-record).
phase_1_handler_extraction.estimated_scope: ~5 tasks (TASK-1-1 through TASK-1-4 in the companion plan, plus the make_gateway_request sys.exit fix folded into TASK-1-3).
phase_1_handler_extraction.gate: ALL existing CLI tests pass unchanged before Phase 2 starts. Pure refactor; low rollback risk.

phase_2_mcp_tool_package.description: Build the sandbox/egg_agent_tools/ package: server.py (factory), schemas.py (argparse→JSON schema + overrides), tools/*.py (@tool wrappers with asyncio.to_thread + error wrapping + cli_command attribute), bootstrap.py (programmatic nudge from TOOL_NAMESPACES).
phase_2_mcp_tool_package.test_approach: Registration test asserts every handler has a matching @tool registration and vice versa. Each @tool wrapper tested for: (a) successful invocation returns serialised handler dict, (b) handler exception → {is_error: True, content: [...]} tool-result (NOT agent crash), (c) cli_command attribute introspection works for the drift test.
phase_2_mcp_tool_package.gate: `build_sandbox_mcp_server()` returns a server object with exactly 15 registered tool names matching the iteration_1_tool_list above.

phase_3_client_wire_up.description: Wire build_sandbox_mcp_server() + SYSTEM_PROMPT_NUDGE into shared/egg_agent/client.py::run_agent_async behind the EGG_MCP_TOOLS flag.
phase_3_client_wire_up.test_approach: tests/shared/egg_agent/test_client.py extended: (a) EGG_MCP_TOOLS unset → options.mcp_servers untouched, options.system_prompt unchanged (byte-identical to today). (b) EGG_MCP_TOOLS=true → options.mcp_servers['egg'] is the server object, options.system_prompt ends with SYSTEM_PROMPT_NUDGE. (c) can_use_tool callback correctly passes mcp__egg__* tool names through (doesn't spuriously block them).
phase_3_client_wire_up.gate: Flag-off path assertion is byte-identical via dict diff.

phase_4_tests.description: Unit + CI tests for the new surface: handler unit tests, @tool wrapper tests (incl. error path), server factory test, symmetric prompt-nudge drift test, argparse-to-schema derivation test, CLI-MCP drift test, SDK import smoke test.
phase_4_tests.test_approach: Offline fakes/mocks of gateway and SDK. No real claude-agent-sdk network call in unit tests. Integration test gated behind @pytest.mark.integration.
phase_4_tests.gate: All tests green in CI for both flag states.

phase_5_docs.description: docs/reference/agent-tools.md documents the 15-tool surface with schemas, CLI mapping, EGG_MCP_TOOLS flag, EGG_HARNESS=egg caveat. docs/guides/sdlc-pipeline.md adds an 'Agent MCP tools' section. sandbox/agent-config/rules/environment.md documents EGG_MCP_TOOLS for human operators.

phase_6_sdk_pin_and_changelog.description: Pin claude-agent-sdk in sandbox/pyproject.toml and sandbox/Dockerfile (per risk-analyst R2 / reviewer_plan non-blocking); add the SDK-surface smoke test; note the new EGG_MCP_TOOLS env var + tool surface in the changelog.
phase_6_sdk_pin_and_changelog.test_approach: Smoke test imports claude_agent_sdk.{create_sdk_mcp_server, tool} at collection time. Fails CI loudly on an SDK bump that removes or renames either symbol.

acceptance_criteria_mapping.AC1_fresh_agent_knows_tools_without_expl: Met by (a) 15 mcp__egg__* tools appearing in the SDK's native tool-discovery surface on agent spawn (no manual exploration), and (b) the programmatically-rendered SYSTEM_PROMPT_NUDGE listing them explicitly in the first system-prompt turn. Phase-4 tests assert both paths.
acceptance_criteria_mapping.AC2_refine_first_12_min_pattern_disappea: Met by mcp__egg__phase_get_context returning role/phase/tasks/artifacts in one structured call — replaces the 5-tool-call archaeology pattern from the issue. Phase-5 integration test asserts a refiner agent's first 3 turns contain at least one mcp__egg__phase_get_context invocation.
acceptance_criteria_mapping.AC3_new_cli_surfaces_automatically: Met: adding a handler + a @tool wrapper in the relevant namespace file is a two-file diff inside sandbox/egg_agent_tools/. Schema is auto-derived from argparse (schemas.py) with per-tool overrides. The prompt nudge regenerates from TOOL_NAMESPACES at next import. CI drift test (tests/tools/test_mcp_cli_drift.py) asserts every tool with cli_command resolves to the same handler as its CLI.
acceptance_criteria_mapping.AC4_argument_validation_at_boundary: Met by create_sdk_mcp_server's schema pipeline: derive_schema_from_argparse produces a JSON schema consumed by the agent harness. Required fields are validated before the handler runs; the agent sees a structured validation error (is_error=True) rather than a Python traceback.
acceptance_criteria_mapping.AC5_works_in_public_and_private: Met by the in-process architecture — zero new network surface for tool dispatch. Handler HTTP calls traverse the same gateway sidecar they do today in both modes. Phase-5 integration test exercises at least one end-to-end tool call in private-mode.
acceptance_criteria_mapping.AC6_existing_clis_keep_working: Met by the refactor-with-extraction pattern: cmd_X becomes a thin adapter around handler X; existing CLI tests pass unchanged; tests/sandbox/test_{contract,orch}_cli_parity.py snapshot tests assert byte-identical stdout + exit codes. Human operators, entrypoint scripts, and bash recovery wrappers see zero change.

risk_handler_extraction_regressions.description: Splitting cmd_X into adapter + handler could regress the shell CLI if argparse edge cases are mis-handled.
risk_handler_extraction_regressions.mitigation: Phase 1 lands the extraction as a pure refactor with no behaviour change. Existing test_brc_cli_args.py and test_overseer_alert_cli.py are the regression net. New snapshot tests in test_{contract,orch}_cli_parity.py lock stdout + exit codes byte-for-byte with committed fixtures. CI must stay green through Phase 1 before Phase 2 starts.

risk_sys_exit_in_async_context.description: contract_cli.py:284/288/291 currently call sys.exit(1) on gateway error. If a handler is called from an @tool async context and that path fires, the agent interpreter exits — the pipeline sees an AGENT_FAILED event. Aligned with risk-analyst R1.
risk_sys_exit_in_async_context.mitigation: TASK-1-3 refactors make_gateway_request to raise GatewayError instead. Handlers MUST never call sys.exit (enforced by grep test in Phase 4: tests/sandbox/egg_agent_tools/test_no_sys_exit.py asserts no sys.exit in any handlers/*.py or tools/*.py file). CLI cmd_* shims catch GatewayError and render the same stderr + exit code for human callers.

risk_blocking_event_loop.description: urllib gateway calls in handlers are synchronous and could block the asyncio event loop for up to 30 seconds if called directly from the @tool async wrapper. Aligned with risk-analyst R1.
risk_blocking_event_loop.mitigation: Every @tool wrapper invokes its handler via asyncio.to_thread(handler, req). Phase-4 test test_tools_use_to_thread greps every tools/*.py file for the asyncio.to_thread call pattern and asserts no direct handler() call in an async def.

risk_claude_agent_sdk_unpinned.description: sandbox/pyproject.toml currently has `claude-agent-sdk` with no version pin. Pre-1.0 SDKs can break between releases — create_sdk_mcp_server, @tool, or ClaudeAgentOptions.mcp_servers could disappear or be renamed. Aligned with risk-analyst R2 and reviewer_plan's non-blocking §dependencies_and_constraints.version_pinning comment.
risk_claude_agent_sdk_unpinned.mitigation: TASK-6-1 pins to `>=0.1.65,<0.2` in pyproject.toml and Dockerfile; test_sdk_surface.py imports the three SDK symbols at collection time so CI fails loudly on an incompatible bump.

risk_prompt_nudge_token_cost.description: Bootstrap nudge adds ~200 input tokens per turn across the agent's session. For a 100-turn agent that's ~20k extra input tokens.
risk_prompt_nudge_token_cost.mitigation: Keep nudge under 200 words. Gated by EGG_MCP_TOOLS — flag-off pipelines pay zero. Observability in Phase 5 measures per-turn input-token cost for on/off A/B during burn-in.

risk_egg_harness_divergence.description: EGG_HARNESS=egg path doesn't see the new tools. Experimental-harness users continue to pay the shell-CLI burn.
risk_egg_harness_divergence.mitigation: Document in docs/reference/agent-tools.md. Per decision-3, parallel registration tracked for iteration 2 when the egg harness graduates. Harness is opt-in and not used in production today.

risk_tool_schema_drift.description: Hand-curated schemas (decision-2 hybrid) could drift from handler signatures or CLI argparse over time.
risk_tool_schema_drift.mitigation: tests/tools/test_mcp_cli_drift.py asserts every tool with cli_command resolves to the same handler as its CLI. test_prompt_nudge_drift asserts SYSTEM_PROMPT_NUDGE ↔ TOOL_NAMESPACES bijection (both directions). Schema derivation in schemas.py makes the auto-derived path primary; overrides are per-tool exceptions, reviewed at PR time.

risk_mcp_server_init_latency.description: Creating the MCP server at each agent spawn adds startup time.
risk_mcp_server_init_latency.mitigation: create_sdk_mcp_server is pure Python and fast (no network, no subprocess). Phase-5 e2e test measures spawn-to-first-tool latency; budget <= 100ms overhead.

risk_private_mode_url_leakage.description: A future handler that reaches orchestrator URLs directly (bypassing the gateway) would work in public mode and fail in private mode, creating a mode-dependent behaviour gap.
risk_private_mode_url_leakage.mitigation: Handlers always use GATEWAY_URL (already the pattern in contract_cli.py:27). Unit test grep asserts no direct orchestrator-URL construction in sandbox/egg_agent_tools/handlers/*.py.

risk_rollout_blast_radius.description: Every opted-in pipeline in iteration 1 is exposed to the new tool surface immediately. A bug in one @tool handler could affect every agent role (refiner, planner, architect, coder, reviewer).
risk_rollout_blast_radius.mitigation: EGG_MCP_TOOLS default false (opt-in). Burn-in on 5-10 pipelines per feedback-Q8 before flipping default in a follow-up PR. Per-role allowed_tools filtering is deferred to iteration 2 when role-specific namespaces become differentiated.

TD1_server_namespacing.question: One aggregate SDK MCP server containing all 15 tools, or one server per semantic namespace (sdlc/brc/phase/progress/task)?
TD1_server_namespacing.decision: Single aggregate server named 'egg' containing all 15 tools. Semantic namespace grouping lives at the tool-name prefix level (mcp__egg__sdlc_*, mcp__egg__brc_*, etc.) and in TOOL_NAMESPACES registry.
TD1_server_namespacing.rationale: Aligned with task_planner's final plan (divergence from architect v1). Aggregate server is strictly simpler to wire: ClaudeAgentOptions.mcp_servers takes one dict entry instead of five; the SDK flat tool list is the same. SDK-exposed tool names have the identical `mcp__<server>__<tool>` structure either way. Per-namespace gating (e.g. reviewer-only disables mcp__egg__progress_*) can be added later by splitting the aggregate into per-namespace servers without changing the agent-visible tool_name surface.
TD1_server_namespacing.trade_off_accepted: Loses the minor convenience of `options.mcp_servers['progress'].disable()` at runtime. In practice, gating by per-role build_sandbox_mcp_server(role=...) parameters that filter TOOL_NAMESPACES is equivalent and keeps the one-server shape.

TD2_handler_location.question: Where do the pure handler functions live? sandbox/egg_lib/ (co-located with CLIs) or sandbox/egg_agent_tools/handlers/ (co-located with tool wrappers)?
TD2_handler_location.rationale: Aligned with task_planner's final plan (divergence from architect v1). Co-locating handlers with their @tool wrappers keeps the agent-tool import surface contained in one package, simplifies the drift-prevention CI test (one package to scan for (cli_command, handler_fn) pairs), and keeps the lazy-import boundary in run_agent_async clean (one package to guard behind the flag). CLI argparse dispatchers in sandbox/egg_lib/{contract,orch}_cli.py still call into these handlers from their module boundary — no different from any other Python caller.

TD3_bootstrap_nudge_location.question: Is the nudge generated at orchestrator-side prompt assembly (_build_agent_prompt) or at sandbox-side client construction (run_agent_async)?
TD3_bootstrap_nudge_location.decision: Sandbox-side, in run_agent_async, derived from the TOOL_NAMESPACES registry at module import.
TD3_bootstrap_nudge_location.rationale: The nudge content is a function of the tool registry (the module that actually creates the servers). Coupling it to the orchestrator's prompt builder would require exporting the tool list across the k8s boundary and risks drift between 'what we told the agent exists' and 'what actually registered'. Client-side generation from the live registry means the nudge is always accurate to whatever the current sandbox image registers.

TD4_nudge_source_of_truth.question: Is SYSTEM_PROMPT_NUDGE a markdown file resource, or a Python string generated at import?
TD4_nudge_source_of_truth.decision: Python string rendered from TOOL_NAMESPACES at import time (not a markdown resource file).
TD4_nudge_source_of_truth.rationale: Addresses reviewer_plan non-blocking feedback and risk-analyst R4. A markdown resource is editable by non-Python operators, but it breaks the drift-prevention contract — the registry stops being the single source of truth. Programmatic rendering keeps the 'adding a namespace updates the nudge automatically' property without a second-source edit. If the rendered text needs to be human-readable outside the codebase, a `make docs` target can emit it to docs/reference/agent-tools.md on demand — but the runtime source is Python. The symmetric drift test (test_prompt_nudge_drift) asserts the nudge contains exactly the namespaces TOOL_NAMESPACES declares, in both directions.

TD5_schema_style.question: TypedDict schemas, dict-of-types schemas, or argparse-auto-derived schemas?
TD5_schema_style.decision: Argparse-auto-derived skeleton with per-tool overrides via build_tool_schema(tool_name, overrides). Tools without a CLI counterpart declare their schema directly as JSON-schema dict.
TD5_schema_style.rationale: Matches decision-2 (hybrid auto/override). schemas.derive_schema_from_argparse inspects the existing argparse subparsers in orch_cli.create_parser() and contract_cli.create_parser(), which already encode type/required/help info for every CLI arg. Per-tool overrides handle the cases where argparse help is insufficient (free-form text fields, enum-typed args, etc.). New-capability tools (check_hitl_answers, brc_get_state, brc_list_blocking, phase_get_context, phase_get_assigned_tasks) declare their schema inline since no argparse exists.

TD6_sync_vs_async_handlers.question: Should handlers be natively async (aiohttp) or sync-wrapped-in-to_thread (urllib)?
TD6_sync_vs_async_handlers.decision: Sync handlers with asyncio.to_thread wrap in every @tool wrapper.
TD6_sync_vs_async_handlers.rationale: Existing CLI handlers use urllib.request.urlopen (sync). Rewriting them to aiohttp is out of scope and adds a new runtime dep. asyncio.to_thread is cheap, native, and doesn't block the event loop. Tool latency is dominated by gateway round-trip (tens-to-hundreds of ms), not Python overhead. Phase-4 test asserts every @tool wrapper uses asyncio.to_thread and no handler is called directly from an async def body.

TD7_feature_flag_shape.question: EGG_DISABLE_AGENT_TOOLS (opt-out, default on) or EGG_MCP_TOOLS (opt-in, default off)?
TD7_feature_flag_shape.decision: EGG_MCP_TOOLS with default false (opt-in) for iteration 1.
TD7_feature_flag_shape.rationale: Aligned with task_planner's final plan and risk-analyst R11 preference (divergence from architect v1 TD6). Default-off means no pipeline sees the new tool surface without explicit opt-in during burn-in, limiting blast radius if a handler bug surfaces. Default-off also keeps the off-path byte-identical to today, which is the strongest possible regression guarantee. A follow-up PR flips the default to true (or removes the flag) once the 5–10 pipeline burn-in shows ≥15% reduction in turns-per-phase for refine/plan.

TD8_error_surfacing.question: When a handler raises, does the tool return {is_error: True, content: [...]} or let the exception propagate?
TD8_error_surfacing.decision: Catch and wrap: every @tool wrapper returns {is_error: True, content: [{type: 'text', text: <message>}]} on handler exception.
TD8_error_surfacing.rationale: Letting exceptions propagate kills the agent session — the SDK treats unhandled exceptions as terminal. Wrapping as an MCP tool error lets the agent read the error and recover (retry with different args, surface the failure, escalate via HITL). Consistent with create_sdk_mcp_server example handling in the SDK docs. Phase-4 test asserts: on gateway 5xx, tool returns is_error=True; the surrounding run_agent_async does not crash.

TD9_peer_read_artifact_deferred.question: Should brc_peer_read_artifact (reviewer fetches producer's proposal artifact directly) be in iteration 1 or iteration 2?
TD9_peer_read_artifact_deferred.rationale: The capability is genuinely valuable for forensic BRC review (currently reviewers dig through .egg-state/brc-history/ with Glob/Grep/Read). Per reviewer_plan non-blocking feedback, the burn is 1-2 tool calls rather than the 5+ pattern described in the issue, so it doesn't fit the critical-path threshold for iteration-1 scope (decision-8). The capability is explicitly noted as a #1917 follow-up target so it doesn't fall off the roadmap.

TD10_sdk_pin_policy.question: How do we guard against breaking changes in pre-1.0 claude-agent-sdk releases?
TD10_sdk_pin_policy.decision: Pin to `>=0.1.65,<0.2` in sandbox/pyproject.toml and sandbox/Dockerfile. Add a symbol-level import smoke test (test_sdk_surface.py) that fails CI on an incompatible bump.
TD10_sdk_pin_policy.rationale: Per risk-analyst R2 and reviewer_plan non-blocking feedback. Bare 'claude-agent-sdk' installs the latest; a 0.2.0 that renames create_sdk_mcp_server or changes ClaudeAgentOptions.mcp_servers type would silently break every sandbox at runtime. A bounded range catches this at CI time; the smoke test catches it at test collection time regardless of the pin.

open_questions_for_plan_reviewers_resolv: Q: PR sequencing — one PR or multiple? A: One PR (task_planner plan is explicit). Commits grouped by phase for reviewability.

Q: BOOTSTRAP_NUDGE as Python constant or markdown resource? A: Python (TD4). Programmatic rendering from TOOL_NAMESPACES — markdown resource is emitted on demand by `make docs` for readers, not used at runtime.

Q: Integration-test harness — live SDK session or VCR? A: Integration test is marker-gated @pytest.mark.integration (per task_planner plan TASK-4-7). Offline unit tests use fakes for the common path; live is opt-in in CI.

Q: shared/tests/test_egg_harness/test_client.py vs sandbox/tests/ ownership? A: sandbox tests own registration-level assertions; shared tests own only the mcp_servers propagation through run_agent_async.
explicit_non_goals: Deprecating any sandbox/bin/egg-* CLI (decision-4: keep indefinitely).
Registering tools in the EGG_HARNESS=egg path (decision-3: deferred to iteration 2).
Exposing orchestrator-admin tools (submit_task / cancel_task / restart_phase) to sandbox agents — these must remain unreachable.
Shipping the full ~30-tool capability audit — iteration 2 is #1917 (peer, checkpoint, anchor, overseer, task-gap verbs).
Changing the orchestrator's mcp_server.py or mcp_tools.py — different surface, different consumer.
Adding a new network port, sidecar, or k8s Service — in-process is the whole point.
Flipping EGG_MCP_TOOLS default to true in this PR — burn-in first, follow-up PR flips default.
Per-role allowed_tools filtering — deferred to iteration 2 when role-specific namespaces become differentiated.
Auto-generating tool schemas end-to-end from argparse reflection — hybrid means we inspect argparse where it suffices but allow hand-override (decision-2).
success_criteria: A fresh sandbox agent on a refine phase issues a single mcp__egg__phase_get_context call in its first 3 turns (vs the 5-tool-call archaeology baseline from the issue).
mcp__egg__* tool_use events appear in checkpoint logs with distinct tool names (observable via `egg-checkpoint list --tool mcp__egg__brc_propose`).
All existing sandbox/tests/ and integration_tests/ tests pass unchanged.
No new long-running process, no new port, no new k8s Service.
Flag-off pipeline (EGG_MCP_TOOLS unset) is byte-identical to today — dict-level diff of ClaudeAgentOptions.
Flag-on pipeline successfully invokes every iteration-1 tool end-to-end in private mode (verified in integration_tests/test_sandbox_mcp_tools_e2e.py).
claude-agent-sdk is pinned in sandbox/pyproject.toml and sandbox/Dockerfile; test_sdk_surface.py verifies symbol availability at collection time.
Burn-in metrics collected on 5-10 pipelines with flag on, feeding a follow-up PR's default-flip decision.
